publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: In the interfacial diffusion method, an additive is mixed into the semiconducting layer and then diffused into the insulation during the cross-linking high-temperature process. In order to investigate the stability of additive concentration, model cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cables were prepared and aged by heating. The additive concentration distribution was measured by micro-beam infrared spectrometry. From the temporal change of distribution, the diffusion coefficient, the activation energy, etc. were analyzed. It was found that the additive concentration profile in the insulation is formed under the influence of the additive concentration distribution. The stability of the additive concentration distribution was estimated after long-term utilization because of the existence of a high molecular weight part which had a small diffusion coefficient in the additive.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Polarization phenomena in AC aged XLPE cable in humid environment
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: The origin of electrical ageing of XLPE (cross-linked polyethylene) with AC field in a humid environment was investigated. Specifically, a comprehensive study of the dielectric polarization of XLPE power distribution cables, immersed in water and under AC electrical stress, was conducted using thermally stimulated discharge current (TSDC) and thermal transient current (TTC) studies. The initial results of the TSDC and TTC measurements are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effectiveness of admixturing treatment of aged transformer oils
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: The effectiveness of admixturing treatment is considered in the macroscopic formulation. This maintenance activity consists of the insertion of a small amount of suitable organic acid (not more than 0.1% by weight) to partially aged transformer oil in due time. The admixturing effects are evaluated by means of tan delta measurements made for oils in service. The effectiveness of the admixturing treatment depends on the electrical parameters of power transformers and seems to be especially satisfactory for MV transformer units. From field investigations it appears that tan delta mean values of admixtured oils may decrease temporarily by several times and the long-term admixturing effects are justified by the substantial prolongation of the operating time of certain transformer units.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Substituent effect on dielectric properties of substituted cobalt phthalocyanine complexes
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: The effect of varying frequency, temperature and end groups on the dielectric properties of four substituted monomeric cobalt phthalocyanine complexes was studied over the range 100 Hz to 1 MHz 40 degrees C-160 degrees C. The dielectric constant was shown to increase with increasing temperature and decreasing frequency. Complexes with imido end groups show a low dielectric constant on the order of 10, while complexes with carboxylic end groups show high dielectric constants on the order of 10/sup 3/-10/sup 4/. Thus, nomadic polarization effects in the phthalocyanine macrocycle seem to be significantly modified by different substituents.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Breakdown characteristics of rod-plane gap under salt fog for AC and DC voltages
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: AC and DC breakdown test results are presented for rod-plane gaps under salt fog. It is found that, in general, there may be no significant change in the breakdown values of the gaps even under severe saline pollution in case of both AC and DC voltages. The breakdown voltage values are, however, very much lower in the case of DC negative voltages under salt fog conditions than under dry conditions. This may be one of the reasons for the arc bridging of the underribs of a polluted insulator under DC negative voltages.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The electric strength of the air polluted by industrial dust
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: The author presents results of laboratory tests carried out on the electric strength at 50 Hz of air polluted by industrial dust at different values of air humidity. The results clearly indicate that the importance of the influence of industrial dust on the electric strength of aerial gaps has been underestimated. It is necessary to initiate further research on this problem, especially as far as bigger spark gaps are concerned. The relation between the electric strength of the air and the degree of its humidity is shown to change in an atmosphere polluted by industrial dust.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement of spatial distributions of mobility and conductivity in electron-beam-irradiated PMMA
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: Spatial distributions of electric field intensity, mobility, and electric conductivity in PMMA can be obtained by combining the volume charge distribution measured using the pulsed electroacoustic method, the current continuity equation, and Poisson's equation. The exact measurement of charge distribution and its decay with respect to time allows the measurement of spatial distribution of mobility and conductivity due to the remaining charge after e-beam irradiation. For electron beam energies of 0.5, 0.75, 1.00 and 1.25 MeV on the PMMA sample, distributions of charge density, electric field intensity, mobility and conductivity depended on the electron beam energy. For sample temperatures of 27, 40, 60 and 80 degrees C, these distributions were also obtained. Charge mobility in the sample became uniform as the sample temperature increased. At high temperature, volume charges were thermally excited and moved easily. Therefore, the mobility and conductivity increased with increasing sample temperature.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study on the leakage current characteristics of the salt contaminated insulators
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: Indications of different degrees of salt contamination were obtained experimentally in order to estimate the occurrence of flashover in insulators. These data are then used to find a method for estimating the best period and the most suitable data for recoating silicone grease. Preliminary experimental results are presented on the effective life of silicone grease coating for preventing salt contamination. The experimental results clearly indicate that, when voltage is applied to a contaminated insulator, the through leakage current is not low even for a slightly contaminated insulator, but its waveform is normal. If the value of contamination is increased, a pulsed current component appears in its current waveform.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fuzzy clustering for diagnosis in electrical insulation
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: Fuzzy clustering is applied to the corona pulse test method. The corona degradation of transformers was evaluated using this approach, and the validity of fuzzy clustering theory in this connection is discussed. The development of this approach is then examined, and results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Theoretical and empirical error analysis for the direct calibration of resonant partial discharge detection circuitry
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: An approximate expression for the inherent error associated with the direct calibration of conventional resonant PD (partial discharge) measurement circuitry has been derived. This relation defines an equivalent charge transfer ratio (ECTR), i.e. the ratio between actual and nominal charges transferred to an insulation test specimen, which explicitly shows the dependence of the direct calibration error on the magnitude of the calibrator coupling capacitor and the stray capacitance of the PD detection network. If the parasitic test loop capacitance is carefully estimated, then the ECTR can be determined and the direct calibration data scaled accordingly to yield a superior calibration. The expression is used to calculate the percent error for the calibration of a commercial resonant PD detector that is typical of industrial apparatus, and the results are compared to laboratory measurements and a computer model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Permittivity measurements on molecular-sized samples
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: Experimental and instrumental design is described in connection with efforts to make organic bistable devices. One of the research goals is to measure the electrical properties of materials and active devices made with molecular (mainly organic) materials. The size of material samples, and the specimens used for measurement, are exceedingly small, typically layers with a thickness on the order of 100 nm. Preliminary results on polyethylene crystals grown under properly controlled circumstances from solutions of PE in xylene are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Charging and discharging of Lexan in vacuum
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: Lexan (polycarbonate) samples cut from commercially available sheets were equipped with vacuum-evaporated aluminum electrodes, and subjected to voltages of 1000 V and either 3000 or 5000 V. The charging and discharging currents were measured from a starting time of 15 s after voltage application to 1000 s. The electrode configuration allowed both surface and bulk currents. By changing the size of the electrodes, the total current was separated into perimeter-dependent and area-dependent terms. The experiments were carried out in vacuum and samples were kept in vacuum for various lengths of time to observe the effects of loss of volatiles on the measured currents. The effect of the vacuum aging on the currents 60 s after the step voltage was applied for a soap-cleaned sample was evaluated. The results indicate that sample-to-sample differences are more important than vacuum aging.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of dissolved water in dielectric liquid included gas on electrical conduction
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: The states of water dissolved in the liquid dielectric di-octyl-phthalate (DOP) were analyzed using the infrared (IR) absorption spectra of water measured by Fourier-transform IR. The states of water in DOP are shown to be independent of the gas impurities, as well as independent of the stress. The H/sub 2/O molecules are classified into monomer, dimer and trimer, and the formation is independent of the dissolved gas in DOP. Monomers do not contribute to the conduction whereas the conduction depends on the amount of dimer and trimer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prebreakdown imaging in continuously stressed n-hexane
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: Prebreakdown imaging in continuously stressed n-hexane reveals that, in addition to the normally expected negative point discharge, there are two completely isolated positive point events. The commonly observed positive point streamer is supersonic and filamentary, and the associated current has a ramped wavefront and is often followed by a series of fast but relatively widely separated pulses. The anomalous positive point event has a subsonic propagation speed, a bush-shaped image profile, and a discrete pulsed conduction current characteristic that strongly resembles the negative point case.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Insulation problems for lunar electrical transmission lines
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: Initial models of lunar transmission lines have provided insight into the effects of various design parameters on size, mass and operating temperatures. Most likely, high-power lines transmitting over a few km will use moderately high voltages (1-10 kV). The insulation of such voltages in the lunar environment will be a significant challenge, requiring new insulation designs. Both solid-dielectric and vacuum insulation have been considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical investigations of the recovery phase for impulse breakdown on the submicrosecond time range
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: An optical investigation of the recovery phase of SF/sub 6/ and the SF/sub 6/-N/sub 2/ gas mixture in the submicrosecond time range is presented. One aim of the investigations was the evaluation of the maximum repetition rate which can be realized using a spark gap as a closing switch. A high-voltage pulse generator was used, which delivers multiple square wave pulses with a constant time interval to allow recovery. For the analysis of the recovery phase, a high-speed photographic system was used, providing framing with a high spatial resolution. It is shown that, for the parameters considered, a recovery phase of 400 ns after a duration of current flow from 20 ns to 380 ns is not sufficient for reaching the original dielectric strength.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Temperature distribution in the dielectric insulation of distribution cables
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: A theoretical model is developed to accurately determine the rise in the temperature of the core, the dielectric insulation, and the soil surrounding a single-phase distribution cable. The model is capable of predicting the temperature distribution as a function of electric current and cable properties. The model is validated experimentally for an XLPE (cross-linked polyethylene) distribution cable. The temperature of the insulation of the cable in the ground is higher than that of the cable in air for the same current level. The particular cable used can carry up to 1.2 of the rated current in air without exceeding the maximum allowable temperature.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effects of natural zeolite filler on tracking in paper phenolic laminate
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: In order to improve tracking failure, natural zeolite was used as filler in paper phenolic laminate. The X-ray diffraction pattern of the natural zeolite clearly shows the mineral structure. The main mineral is clinoptilolite. This zeolite structure was maintained at test temperatures up to 450 degrees C. The improvement of the resistance to tracking in the natural-zeolite-filled paper phenolic laminate with 0.5 wt.% to 5.0 wt.% was investigated by a test method similar to the IEC tracking test. From the experimental results obtained by the IEC tracking test for copper electrodes, on the basis of comparative indices in the unfilled sample, the increasing percentages of comparative indices in samples with 0.5 wt.% to 5.0 wt.% are about 11% to 37%.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comments on the electrotechnical ageing compensation effect
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: In many cases of accelerated thermal aging of polymeric materials of electrical interest, for various Arrhenius lifelines corresponding to various properties of a given material, to various materials with the same endlife criterion, and to various endlife criteria for a given material, a linear correlation exists between the logarithm of the preexponential factor and the activation energy. An attempt is made to demonstrate that, in many important cases, the existence of such a correlation, called the compensation effect, results from the non-Arrhenian character of the kinetics. An experimental and a numerical example show that, for an aging process resulting from two successive steps, the non-Arrhenian kinetics leads to an apparent compensation effect. Another experimental and numerical example shows that, for a sequential process, an apparent compensation effect can also be observed in a comparative study of various materials of close composition.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of disc-type spacers on the breakdown characteristics of a coaxial cylindrical SF/sub 6/ gas-gap under direct voltages with superimposed alternating voltages
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: The authors report the breakdown characteristics of a coaxial cylindrical SF/sub 6/-filled gas-gap as well as the surface flashover characteristics of disk-type spacers subjected to pulsating DC voltage of either polarity superimposed on 50-Hz alternating voltage. In the pressure range of 0.1 to 0.2 MPa, the breakdown strength is almost independent of pressure, and for pressures above 0.2 MPa the breakdown strength decreases at a constant rate with increasing pressure, suggesting that the streamer mechanisms may be at work. As the percentage of superimposed AC component in the applied pulsating positive direct voltage increases, the peak BDV and FOV decrease; this effect is opposite for negative polarity. With negative polarity, the peak BDV and FOV are lower than those for positive polarity for superimposed AC components less than 100%.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical properties of metal-Langmuir-Blodgett (LB)-metal devices
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: Fundamental electrical properties are investigated for metal-asymmetrical Langmuir-Blodgett (LB) film-metal devices using thermally stimulated currents (TSCs). Alternate-layer LB films of merocyanine (MC) dyes and fatty acids (FAs) are deposited. The orientations of MC molecules are in opposite directions with respect to the substrate. Pyroelectric currents whose directions depend on the orientations of MC molecules are observed between 100 and 300 K without application of bias voltages. In addition, TSC peaks due to dipolar polarization are observed below room temperature. Pyroelectric currents that remarkably increase with temperature above approximately 330 K are observed in the first heating stages for the two types of films. The directions of the currents also depend on the types of LB films, and they are the same for currents below room temperature. The results indicate that positive charges easily transfer from MC head groups to adjacent FA head groups in the heating stages, or that negative charges easily transfer from FA to MC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Instability criteria at interface regions of spherical cavities in solid dielectric cable
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: Charge formation and the associated electric field distribution is described for a spherical cavity embedded in solid dielectric cable are treated analytically. This model is useful for understanding the high-voltage breakdown process in dielectric materials. Emphasis is placed on understanding the role of various phenomena at the cavity interface. The effects of space charge, discharge, polarization, and charge relaxation are considered. The analysis is based electrically on Poisson's equation and, kinematically on the diffusion transport mechanism. The interaction between the gaseous plasma in the cavity and the dielectric surface is critical. The prebreakdown mechanism at the gaseous/dielectric interface is linked to the argument (K nu *r/sub 2/). K nu is a degrading factor related to the dynamic interaction between partial discharge and the dielectric surface, and r/sub 2/ is the cavity size. Dielectric instability at the interface increases with r/sub 2/ and decreases inversely with K nu . Instability implies degradation at the interface due to local field enhancement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Method for unambiguous recognition of slot discharge in rotating machines
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: A procedure which allows one to detect and localize dangerous slot discharges at a very early state is described. This procedure for evaluating the aging state of the insulating system in rotating machines consists of a sequence of steps with increasing complexity of the diagnostic tools and also with increasing cost for the steps to be performed. The decision to proceed with the next step is mainly based on the experience of the engineers involved in the diagnostics. It is pointed out that more field experience with this procedure is necessary to build up a knowledge base to allow fast and correct analysis of the results obtained at each step of the procedure. Typical results obtained with on-site measurements on power generators are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Degradation of silicone-coated FRP by weathering
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: To estimate the quality of sample coating materials, a merit index was calculated from the average value of the order in flashover voltages and the contact angle of the sample insulator during exposure. The contact angle is shown to be the most effective factor for the degradation of sample instructors. Under wet conditions, a low contact angle causes creeping discharges resulting in tracking.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new fog chamber testing technique for anti-contamination distribution insulators
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: In order to evaluate the performance of anti-contamination distribution insulators, a novel testing procedure was developed taking into account the characteristics of these types of insulators. This testing procedure, which allows one to evaluate the operating limits of the anti-contamination insulators, is described in detail. To show the convenience of the method, experimental results from an actual test are presented. From these results, it can be inferred that the tested insulator will perform satisfactorily in heavily polluted areas. Moreover, the results can serve to compare the performance of this insulator with that of other insulator designs such as resistive graded.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dependence of dielectric constant of n-alkanes on free volume
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: A relation between relative dielectric constant and fractional free volume (FFV) of nonpolar condensed matter was previously developed by the authors using the Clausius-Mosotti equation together with free volume theory. A comparison of this relation with a large body of experimental data collected from the literature is given. It is concluded that this relation coincides quite satisfactorily with the characteristics of n-alkanes (from C/sub l/ to C/sub l2/) over a wide range of temperatures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The universal dielectric response
publicationTitle: Annual Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena
abstract: A brief description is given of the various manifestations of the universal fractional power law relaxation processes, which are contrasted with the classical or Debye law. It is shown that the universal law is indeed found in a remarkable variety of physical and chemical situations, and this is deemed to merit a special attempt at finding a suitably general theoretical model. Several such models are briefly described, and a novel very general approach based on the so-called energy criterion is introduced. It is concluded that it is not yet possible to establish with certainty the validity of any of the models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
